chapter: Postwar records, Miami and Los Angeles
title: Betty Riley insists on making the film with Machito's black band
summary: Studio objected to a white girl with a black band, but she insisted on Machito because he played the real thing.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: So when we come back to New York, she was waiting for us, for that particular .....
So that's 1946, when you made it.

Nineteen forty-six; so she was waiting for us. In those days, you know, discrimination problem, or whatever, and they don't want her to make the picture with us because we were going to be banned in a lot of states in the United States.
*Cabildo is a particular Afro-Cuban religious cult of rather exclusive membership.
Because she was a white girl.

She was a white girl and we was a black band. So she say: 'I don't care if they don't show this picture in Georgia or whatever, I want to make this picture with Machito because Machito play the real thing. If I can't make it with Machito, forget it'., and they were very impressed because she was blond, good voice, good personality, good singer and they thought that it could -- there was a team a dance team that it was dancing mambo, you know, those exhibition things......
